title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool & parallel calls, result injection, and retry policies
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: make tool-calling ergonomics robust for real production workflows: allow multiple tool calls within a single execution, support parallel tool execution with deterministic result injection order, surface partial tool outputs over streaming, and introduce per-tool retry policies with idempotency hooks. This PR touches the OpenAI-compat shim, API layer, serving runtime executor, SDK examples, and docs. High-level changes: 1) Execution graph: introduce a lightweight DAG-based execution plan for coordinating multi-tool and parallel calls; deterministic injection order is configurable (by schedule/priority or call-order). 2) Streaming: stream tool partial results as tool-output chunks to the client and to the model (prefix injection) with backpressure handling to avoid head-of-line blocking. 3) Tool result injection: new injection points (pre-token, mid-stream, post-tool) and templates for mapping tool outputs to model messages; injection uses stable placeholders to help evals. 4) Retries: per-tool retry config (max_retries, backoff_ms, retry_on) and idempotency_token support so retries are safe for non-idempotent tools. 5) OpenAI compatibility: add new fields to the compat layer (tool_execution_plan, tool_retry) preserved in request/response but backward-compatible with older clients. 6) Observability + tracing: emit tool_call.{start,success,failure,retry} metrics, add trace spans to show parallel tool durations and injection latency. 7) Tests & examples: e2e tests for parallel calls, unit tests for executor ordering, SDK examples (python/ts) demonstrating multi-tool flows. Checklist: - [x] design doc + Linear tickets (ENG-4821) - [x] API changes and compat shim updates - [x] runtime executor & streaming changes - [x] SDK examples + docs - [x] unit/e2e tests - [x] rollout plan and feature flag (default on for internal fleets, opt-in for external via feature flag) Related: earlier tool-calling PRs pr-20876, pr-21845, pr-22412 for baseline ergonomics; this PR builds on those by adding multi-tool orchestration and retries. Rollout: gated behind feature flag tool_calling_v2; gradual rollout to Dedicated customers then hosted fleet. Impact: improves latency for parallelizable tool workloads; adds small CPU overhead for planning but reduces overall end-to-end latency in common cases. Backwards compatibility: compat shim keeps older fields intact; clients that don't set tool_execution_plan continue to get previous semantics (serial tool execution).
commit_summary: Add execution-plan orchestration, streaming tool-output injection, per-tool retry configs, OpenAI-compat fields, observability and tests
review_comments: Arjun: Can we guarantee deterministic ordering for injection when clients request parallel tool calls? Please add a unit test for priority-based ordering.
Maya: We added deterministic scheduling modes: call-order, priority, and explicit sequence. Unit tests added for all three modes (executor_test.go).
Elliot: Streaming backpressure looked risky — what prevents a slow tool from blocking the main chat stream?

Maya: Parallel executor forwards partial tool chunks to the client and model stream; if downstream backpressure occurs we buffer up to a bounded limit and emit backpressure metrics. The feature is guarded by a feature flag and default buffer is conservative.
Sofia: How are retries exposed to SDKs? Need idempotency examples for webhooks and external HTTP tools.
Maya: Added SDK helpers that accept idempotency_token and updated examples; docs include recommended patterns for non-idempotent endpoints.
Arjun: CI failing lint on first run (openai-compat formatting).
Maya: Fixed formatting and re-ran tests; all CI checks now green.
Elliot: Approved after adding an integration test that simulates a flaky external tool and validates backoff/retry semantics.
Sofia: Approved — docs look good and examples are helpful.
release_notes: Improved tool calling ergonomics: supports multi-tool and parallel tool execution with deterministic injection ordering, streaming of partial tool outputs, per-tool retry policies with idempotency tokens, and OpenAI-compat additions. Feature gated by tool_calling_v2. See docs/tool-calling-exec-ergonomics.md for migration and examples.
